steps.what: Review students' fieldwork, internship or research evidence against agreed goals
Observe the student's actual practice or research process
Supervise the student through questions, feedback and agreed next actions
Write factual supervision points and agreed next actions
Write and correct the supervision feedback record

loop.purpose: Draft readable supervision feedback from the lecturer's factual notes
loop.input: Factual observations, attributed student explanations and agreed next actions
loop.output: Draft supervision feedback linked to the notes
loop.check: The lecturer verifies each observation, distinction between observation and interpretation, and agreed action against the notes and corrects the final text
loop.stop: Missing evidence, changed meaning or an invented judgement returns the feedback to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Individual supervision feedback varies beyond fixed headings; native layouts are tried first

steps.what: Send the final supervision feedback to the student

tasks.design: Use a native supervision portfolio view in {LMS} and test its feedback layout before adding a bounded prose draft from lecturer-written notes in {DOCS}. Keep observation and coaching human, retain explicit source-note capture and final text correction, and release the exact feedback in a separate step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Portfolio navigation and turning brief supervision points into readable feedback repeat across students.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and instructor-note feedback drafting can reduce those operations.
tasks.still_hard: A polished account can hide a weak observation or misstate a student explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The lecturer sees the student's actual work and chooses a useful teaching response.
tasks.altitude: Less feedback prose leaves a little more time for direct supervision; assessment authority stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes; this supports drafting capability, not an observed supervision saving.
The supervision workflow and time allowance are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes portfolio review, observation, coaching, factual notes, the actual feedback record and its release. This is supervision feedback rather than separate course-grade evaluation in6151.

The student supplies the portfolio; the lecturer produces observation and agreed-action notes in s4, whose five hours remain fully counted. Required fields are student, activity date, observed action, attributed explanation and next action. Retained18 review and12 feedback-writing hours count source checks and final correction. Missing notes force manual writing.
Test native views and feedback layouts before custom drafting. No ambient recording, performance inference, automated grade or machine release is introduced.
The lecturer's ordinary record save has no self-approval gate or saving. The student-facing release is a separate gated action and retains all five hours.
unknowns: Whether factual notes are sufficient without duplicating note-taking
research_questions: Does note-based drafting save time after every feedback claim and action is checked?

tasks.short: Evaluate assignments and provide checked feedback

steps.what: Read students' assignments and papers against the actual assessment criteria
Evaluate the evidence and determine each grade
Enter grades and factual marking reasons in the assessment record
Write and correct the individual rubric feedback

loop.purpose: Draft feedback wording from the lecturer's existing marking notes
loop.input: Recorded grade, criterion-specific marking reasons and relevant submission passages
loop.output: Draft individual feedback with source references
loop.check: The lecturer checks every criterion, quotation, explanation and suggested improvement against the submission and their own judgement; the model cannot change the grade
loop.stop: Missing passage support, conflicting reasons or changed judgement returns feedback to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Individual explanatory prose varies beyond reusable rubric headings

steps.what: Release the final grade and checked feedback to the student

tasks.design: Use native rubric-entry fields in {LMS}, then draft feedback wording from the lecturer's recorded reasons through a bounded loop. Reading, grading and all final feedback checks remain human, with the result released in its own step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lecturers repeatedly enter criterion headings and expand marking notes into feedback prose.
tasks.enabler_now: Native rubric forms and note-based feedback drafting can shorten that clerical and wording work.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible comment may not fairly explain the student's work or the awarded grade.
tasks.human_edge: The lecturer judges educational reasoning and gives an appropriate next learning step.
tasks.altitude: Less feedback wording can support clearer individual explanations; the lecturer retains each grade decision.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts feedback from instructor notes, supporting a wording-assistance workflow.
The Michigan feedback trial reported better revisions and no time data; it does not establish this saving.
The local decomposition and time allowances are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes submission reading, grading, actual marking-record entry, feedback writing and student release. A second institutional grade-register rekey, if present, must be measured separately and earns no saving here.

Students produce submissions and the existing course process produces the rubric. The lecturer produces grades, criterion reasons and relevant passage references in s2-s3; s3 retains eight hours for actual capture and checks. s4 retains12.5 hours for source and meaning correction. Missing reasons or passage support require manual feedback.
Test native rubrics and reusable comments before a model. No automated grade, applicant selection, fraud judgement or grade publication is introduced.
Ordinary author saves have no self-approval gate or saving. The student-facing release has its own final-version gate and retains all five hours.
research_questions: Does note-based feedback drafting save time after every comment is checked against the submission?

approvals.approved_version: The exact final grade, corrected feedback, submission and student recipient checked before release; any edit voids release

steps.what: Choose lecture objectives and the teaching problem to address
Check readings and existing materials for the education topic
Choose the lecture argument, examples and learning sequence
Prepare slides, teaching notes and examples for the lectures

loop.purpose: Draft slide and note wording within a lecturer-chosen outline
loop.input: Chosen lecture outline and checked source excerpts
loop.output: Draft lecture materials with source references and marked illustrative examples
loop.check: The lecturer checks educational claims, examples, source attribution and fit to the chosen argument; invented citations and unsupported claims are removed
loop.stop: Missing support or a distorted concept returns the section to manual preparation
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining varied education concepts requires prose beyond a slide template; template reuse is tried first

steps.what: Check the full lecture for accuracy, coherence and accessibility
Deliver the lecture and respond to students' questions

tasks.design: Reuse native course-source links in {LMS} and a lecture layout in {DOCS}, then draft wording only within a lecturer-selected outline. Source selection, argument, full lecture checking and live teaching remain explicit human steps; no automatic material publication is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source navigation and repeated slide wording consume preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded source-grounded draft can shorten wording without choosing the lecture's argument.
tasks.still_hard: A fluent explanation can obscure contested evidence or teach a misleading simplification.
tasks.human_edge: The lecturer links the material to educational practice and adapts to student questions.

ambition.what: Prepare an accessible companion explanation for students who need extra concept support, after testing the core workflow

tasks.altitude: Less routine wording can support better examples and clearer live explanation.

evidence.claim: The digest's EduGenAI pilot shows an institutional teaching chat platform exists; it does not measure lecture preparation or prove local suitability.
The bounded lecture-drafting workflow and time estimate are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes objectives, source review, outline, actual lecture materials, full checking and live delivery. It adds no lecture transcript or teaching log. The companion explanation is an ambition, not counted in the same-output saving.

The lecturer produces objectives in s1, checks source identity and relevant excerpts in s2 and produces the outline in s3; all30 baseline hours are retained except1.5 navigation hours. s4 retains13.75 hours for drafting, example creation and source checks, with the full10-hour lecture review in s5. Missing sources or disputed interpretations use manual preparation.
Try native source links, reusable slides and layouts before a model. No free reading summary, research bibliography or learning-level metadata is assumed.
Ordinary author saves have no self-approval gate or saving. Live delivery is gated on the checked final lecture and retains35 hours; no separate LMS publish is proposed.
unknowns: Approved teaching-model environment and existing slide reuse
Actual share of wording versus intellectual design
research_questions: Does a source-bounded draft shorten preparation after conceptual and accessibility checks?

steps.what: Write focused discussion prompts from the class topic and learning goal
Present the final prompts to the class
Initiate, facilitate and moderate classroom discussions
Summarize the discussion's reasoning and unresolved questions with the class

tasks.design: Reuse tested question structures from the existing {DOCS} prompt bank when writing the actual discussion prompts. Keep prompt presentation, moderation and the spoken synthesis human; no recording or discussion-summary document is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Familiar question structures are rewritten even when only the education example changes.
tasks.enabler_now: A native prompt bank can remove some repeated framing while preserving topic-specific writing.
tasks.still_hard: The lecturer must notice an unclear argument, exclusion or a misconception in real time.
tasks.human_edge: The lecturer chooses when to challenge, invite another voice or let a productive disagreement develop.
tasks.altitude: A small preparation saving leaves classroom facilitation intact.

evidence.claim: An existing prompt bank can reduce repeated question framing; live facilitation and synthesis remain human.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual prompt writing, its presentation, live moderation and spoken synthesis. No routine discussion transcript or post-class record is assumed; lecture materials in6149 are distinct from seminar prompts here.

The lecturer produces the topic and goal and selects and adapts an existing question structure in s1; its11.25 retained hours count all selection, writing and checking. Missing or unsuitable examples require manual prompt writing.
Test the native document prompt bank before code or a model. No student sentiment, participation score or free discussion summary is consumed by automation.
The prompt author's ordinary save has no self-approval gate or saving. The0.5-hour upkeep allowance covers retiring ineffective prompt structures.
unknowns: Whether a useful prompt bank exists and actual repeat-framing time
research_questions: Does reusing question structures shorten preparation without narrowing student reasoning?
